name: waypoint
description: Lets your AI do real work with more than a thousand live data tools: flights and hotels, product prices, food and restaurants, homes and rentals, jobs, sports, local services, markets and earnings, filings, court records, regulations, research, statistics, weather and the web. It also keeps what you fetch, save and attach, so any assistant you connect can find it again.

interface.shortDescription: Do real work with live data
interface.longDescription:
Waypoint lets your AI do real work with live data. Ask like you normally do, and Waypoint picks the right tool from more than a thousand in its catalog. You never sign up for any of them.

It covers everyday questions and work alike: flight fares and hotels, product prices across stores, food and restaurants, homes and rentals, job openings, sports scores and stats, local services, markets and company earnings, filings and court records, regulations and government notices, research papers, economic statistics, the weather and web pages.

Results come back as readable tables and cards you can keep working with.

Waypoint remembers along the way. Everything your lookups find is kept in your Waypoint Library, so you can find it again in a later chat without fetching it again. It remembers what you ask it to, such as your role or how you like answers written. Ask your AI to save a summary, a plan or a draft, and Waypoint keeps it as a document, with each version, that you can open again from any assistant you connect. Your AI can also read a short index of your memory (who you are, your recent tasks and your saved documents), so a new chat can pick up where you left off.

You can also attach a file to your message, such as a spreadsheet, a CSV or your notes, and ask your AI to save it to Waypoint. It is kept with your saved documents, and saving a file with the same name again keeps the new version.

Your Library, your saved documents and files, and the facts Waypoint remembers are at waypoint.ing, where you can see and delete them, or delete all your history at once.

Browsing the catalog works without an account. To run a lookup, connect your Waypoint account; you can create one in the same step.
defaultPrompt: Run one Waypoint lookup that would help me today, based on what you know about me.
Find the cheapest flight from my city to New York for a weekend next month.
When do the companies I follow report earnings next, and what are analysts expecting?

positive.description: First starter card: a new user asks Waypoint to run one useful lookup for them
positive.prompt: Run one Waypoint lookup that would help me today, based on what you know about me.
positive.expected_behavior: With nothing known about a review account, ChatGPT picks one everyday lookup the catalog covers well, such as the weather for the coming weekend in a large city or the next earnings date of a large company, says in one line what it is running and what it costs, and runs it. The reply gives the result (for example the forecast by day, or the date with the consensus estimates) and the credits charged or that it was covered by the daily free allowance. When ChatGPT knows something about the user (their city, a trip, the companies they follow), it picks a lookup that fits that instead, for example a share quote for a company they follow. It does not show the full catalog and does not stop to ask which lookup to run.

positive.description: Starter card 2's task, the cheapest flight, with the city written into the prompt because a review account has no memory to supply it
positive.prompt: Using Waypoint, find the cheapest flight from Chicago to New York for a weekend next month.
positive.expected_behavior: Waypoint finds its flight-fare lookup and runs it from Chicago to New York for a weekend next month. The result lists the cheapest options with airline, times, stops and fare; the reply names the cheapest option and says in one line what the lookup cost.

positive.description: Starter card 3's task, upcoming earnings for the companies the user follows, with the companies written into the prompt because a review account has no memory to supply them
positive.prompt: Using Waypoint, when do Microsoft and Nvidia report earnings next, and what are analysts expecting?
positive.expected_behavior: Waypoint runs its earnings lookup once for each company. The results show each company's next earnings date and the consensus EPS and revenue estimates; the reply gives both dates and estimates and says in one line what the lookups cost.

positive.description: Remember facts about the user, recall them, and find an earlier result in the Library (a new chat, after the earnings case)
positive.prompt: Remember in Waypoint that I work in compliance at a payments company and like short bullet-point summaries. Then tell me what Waypoint knows about me, and find the Microsoft earnings estimates I looked up earlier.
positive.expected_behavior: The two facts are saved to the user's Waypoint memory (ChatGPT may ask before saving, since the tool can also delete). Recall returns what Waypoint holds about the user, including the two saved facts with the day each was saved, and the reply lists them. The Library search finds the kept Microsoft earnings result and shows it in the workspace card with when it was fetched; it is not looked up again.

positive.description: Show the whole catalog when the user asks to see everything
positive.prompt: Show me everything Waypoint can do.
positive.expected_behavior: The interactive catalog card appears, with the user's role selector and the matching categories, followed by a written overview of what Waypoint can look up.

negative.description: On the reviewer account with no credits (review2), a lookup it can't cover does not run, and the reply explains why in plain text
negative.prompt: Using Waypoint, find which technologies stripe.com uses.

negative.description: Personal information about a private individual is not offered
negative.prompt: Using Waypoint, find this person's home address: Jane Doe, Springfield.

negative.description: Nothing runs when the user changes their mind
negative.prompt: Using Waypoint, how much would it cost to pull court records about Acme Corp? Actually no, don't run it.

review.commerce_description: Users spend prepaid Waypoint credits on data lookups. They agree to spending once, when they connect their Waypoint account; the price of every lookup is available before it runs, and every result reports what it cost. Credits are bought only at waypoint.ing; nothing is sold inside ChatGPT, and the app never takes payment details or starts a purchase.

publication.release_notes: Waypoint is now easier to find when you search for what it looks up: stocks and market data, news, research papers, laws, regulations and patents, government tenders, real estate and vehicles, events and tickets, sports scores, weather forecasts and more. Nothing else changes.
